knowledge_point.title: Differentiating the Product of a Constant and the Natural Logarithm Function

question.:question/worked-solution:
The derivative of the natural logarithm is the reciprocal function:

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\ln x)=\frac{1}{x}
$$

We apply our formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(-\frac{\ln x}{5}\right) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{1}{5}\,\ln x) \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\ln x) \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\  & =-\frac{1}{5x}.\end{aligned}
$$
